title: 304. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Analyzing Graph Intersections
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the coordinates of an intersection point from equal function values.
questions.question: The graphs of \(y=f(x)\) and \(y=g(x)\) intersect at \(x=2\), where \(f(2)=5\) and \(g(2)=5\). Which point is the intersection point?
questions.explanation: An intersection point of two graphs has the form \((x,y)\) where the two \(y\)-values are equal. At \(x=2\), both functions have value \(5\), so the common point is \((2,5)\).
questions.hint: At an intersection, the \(x\)-coordinate is the same and the two \(y\)-values are equal.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the coordinates of an x-axis intersection from a given zero of a function.
questions.question: The graph of \(y=f(x)\) crosses the \(x\)-axis at \(x=-3\). Which point is an intersection of the graph with the \(x\)-axis?
questions.explanation: Every point on the \(x\)-axis has \(y=0\). Since the graph crosses the \(x\)-axis at \(x=-3\), the intersection point is \((-3,0)\).

questions.concept: Solving for an Intersection of Two Lines
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the intersection point of two linear graphs by solving \(f(x)=g(x)\).
questions.question: The graphs of \(f(x)=2x+1\) and \(g(x)=x+4\) intersect at one point. What is the intersection point?
questions.explanation: Set \(2x+1=x+4\). Then \(x=3\). Substituting into either function gives \(y=2(3)+1=7\). Therefore, the intersection point is \((3,7)\).
questions.hint: Set the two function rules equal and solve for \(x\), then find the common \(y\)-value.

questions.concept: Intersections of a Parabola and a Horizontal Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine all intersection points of \(y=x^2\) and \(y=4\).
questions.question: How many intersection points do the graphs of \(y=x^2\) and \(y=4\) have, and what are they?
questions.explanation: Set \(x^2=4\). Then \(x=2\) or \(x=-2\). The corresponding points are \((2,4)\) and \((-2,4)\). Therefore, there are two intersection points.
questions.hint: Solve \(x^2=4\), remembering both positive and negative square roots.

questions.concept: Intersection of a Parabola and a Horizontal Line
questions.learningObjective: Identify one correct intersection point from the equation \(x^2-2x+1=1\).
questions.question: The graphs of \(f(x)=x^2-2x+1\) and \(g(x)=1\) intersect at two points. Which point is one of the intersection points?
questions.explanation: Set \(x^2-2x+1=1\). Then \(x^2-2x=0\), so \(x(x-2)=0\). Thus \(x=0\) or \(x=2\). The intersection points are \((0,1)\) and \((2,1)\). Therefore, \((2,1)\) is an intersection point.
questions.hint: Set the two expressions equal and solve the resulting quadratic equation.

questions.concept: Intersections from a Table of Values
questions.learningObjective: Identify an intersection point by comparing function values in a table.
questions.question:
The table gives values of \(f\) and \(g\):
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3\\
\hline
f(x) & 1 & 4 & 3 & 6\\
g(x) & 3 & 2 & 3 & 5
\end{array}
\]
Which point is an intersection point of the graphs of \(f\) and \(g\)?
questions.explanation: Two graphs intersect where \(f(x)=g(x)\). From the table, \(f(2)=3\) and \(g(2)=3\). Thus the graphs share the point \((2,3)\).
questions.hint: Find an \(x\)-value for which the two table entries are equal.

questions.question: Consider the graphs of \(y=f(x)\) and \(y=f(x)+2\). Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The graphs have no intersection points.

options.label: B
options.text: The graphs intersect at every point where \(f(x)=0\).

questions.explanation: For an intersection, we need \(f(x)=f(x)+2\), which simplifies to \(0=2\). This is impossible for any \(x\). Therefore, the two graphs never intersect.
questions.hint: Set the two \(y\)-expressions equal and see whether the equation can be true.

questions.learningObjective: Relate intersections of \(y=f(x)\) and \(y=-f(x)\) to the zeros of \(f\).
questions.question: The graph of \(y=f(x)\) intersects the graph of \(y=-f(x)\) exactly where \(f(x)=0\). If \(f\) has zeros at \(x=-1\) and \(x=3\), which points are intersection points?
questions.explanation: At an intersection of \(y=f(x)\) and \(y=-f(x)\), we have \(f(x)=-f(x)\), so \(2f(x)=0\), hence \(f(x)=0\). The zeros given are \(x=-1\) and \(x=3\), so the intersection points are \((-1,0)\) and \((3,0)\).
questions.hint: Set \(f(x)\) equal to \(-f(x)\) and solve the resulting condition.

questions.concept: Parameter Condition for Exactly One Intersection
questions.learningObjective: Determine the value of \(k\) for which \(y=x^2\) and \(y=x+k\) have exactly one intersection.
questions.question: For which value of \(k\) do the graphs of \(y=x^2\) and \(y=x+k\) have exactly one intersection point?
questions.explanation:
Set \(x^2=x+k\), so \(x^2-x-k=0\). The graphs have exactly one intersection when this quadratic has exactly one real solution, so its discriminant is zero:
\[
(-1)^2-4(1)(-k)=1+4k=0.
\]
Thus \(k=-\frac{1}{4}\).
questions.hint: Use the discriminant of the quadratic equation obtained by setting the two \(y\)-expressions equal.

questions.concept: Number of Intersections with the x-Axis
questions.learningObjective: Determine the number of intersections of \(y=x^3-3x\) with the \(x\)-axis.
questions.question: How many intersection points does the graph of \(y=x^3-3x\) have with the \(x\)-axis?
questions.explanation:
Intersections with the \(x\)-axis occur where \(y=0\). Solve
\[
x^3-3x=0 \implies x(x^2-3)=0.
\]
Thus \(x=0\), \(x=\sqrt{3}\), and \(x=-\sqrt{3}\). These give three distinct intersection points, so the graph has exactly 3 intersections with the \(x\)-axis.
questions.hint: Set the function equal to zero and factor to find all real solutions.
